Nina —

Thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front:

- We can publish the offer either as a single bundled SKU or as itemized line-items; both are supported by AWS private offers. The tradeoffs are:
  * Bundled SKU: simpler contract mapping (single license), single invoice line; easier for legal but harder for your internal cost-center allocation.
  * Itemized lines: better for your budget owners and internal chargeback; slightly more complex bookkeeping and requires SKU mapping in the private offer.

- Channel margin/commission: Redwood will route reseller commissions as a separate settlement line item. For Nimbus the typical pattern is: Redwood invoices Nimbus at the private-offer net price; the reseller (if applicable) receives commission through our downstream settlement process and any reseller passback or holdback is reconciled monthly. In practice, any credits or passbacks show as a separate credit memo within the next 30–45 days after usage/true-up.

To make this actionable, I proposed a short checklist below and looped Jordan/Ben to confirm the exact wording we should include in the PO and the marketplace listing.

Action checklist (draft):
- Decide SKU structure: bundle vs itemized (state preferred approach)
- Confirm invoicing path: Redwood -> Nimbus (net price) and separate reseller settlement via reseller_id (we'll include reseller_id in the offer metadata)
- Include commission language: commission %, settlement cadence (monthly), and credit memo timing (30–45 days)
- Evidence required: reseller cert, PO + signed SOW if add-ons, proof of committed usage for any tiered discounts
- DocuSign link + timeline: target signature by 2026-09-24 to meet quarter close

Hi all —

Thanks, Laura. Adding some specifics and attaching a compact commission workback (commission_workback_v3.xlsx) for Nimbus to review. High level:

- Recommendation: publish itemized line-items unless Nimbus absolutely cannot accept multiple invoice lines. Reason: it keeps your internal chargeback simple and avoids downstream reconciliation queries during audits. There is a small operational cost (SKU mapping) but we automate most of it.

- Commission math (example):
  * Offer list price per module: M1=$5,000/mo, M2=$2,000/mo
  * Private-offer discount: 20% across all modules
  * Net to Redwood (invoiced to Nimbus): (M1+M2) * 0.8 = $5,600/mo
  * Reseller commission (if reseller engaged) = 10% of list price (or negotiated percent) = (M1+M2) * 0.10 = $700/mo
  * Commission path: reseller commission is tracked off-invoice and settled monthly via our reseller settlement process; Nimbus sees the full net invoice and any reseller-related credits (if applicable) arrive as a credit memo within 30–45 days after invoice date.

- Passback / escrow considerations: if Nimbus needs rapid passback (faster than 30 days) we can propose a carveout with monthly escrow releases — requires approval from finance; raises complexity for private offer acceptance timelines by ~3–5 business days.

- Evidence required for listing & procurement (practical checklist):
  * Signed PO (attached)
  * Reseller cert (if reseller-driven discount)
  * Evidence of committed usage for tiered discounts (if the private offer includes commit bands)
  * Contact for billing reconciliation (we will send a settlement contact email)

I've attached commission_workback_v3.xlsx (attachment stub) that contains the line-by-line math and a sample credit memo we send. If Nimbus wants, Ben can run a one-page pro forma that maps to your internal GL codes.
